Extremely overpriced and not good service
Apr 2026 • Couples
The location on Khem Beach is beautiful, but unfortunately our experience at Anna Seafood was disappointing.
We paid around 2M VND for the meal. 

The squid was very good, but the rest did not justify the price. The oysters were not good, lacked freshness and taste, and were served with “wasabi” that clearly did not seem like real wasabi, so we did not touch it. The biggest disappointment was the live tiger prawns, which were charged at a very high price, around 900k VND for 500g. They were advertised as live, but based on the quality and taste, we honestly doubt they were actually live or as fresh as presented.

The service issue made the experience worse. After spending a lot on food, we asked if we could use one of the beach chairs or ottomans while ordering a few drinks. We were told they were for rent. When we politely explained that we had just eaten there and spent a significant amount, the staff became defensive and aggressive instead of trying to handle the situation professionally.

Overall, the setting is nice and the squid was good, but the seafood quality, value for money, and customer service were poor. For a beach seafood restaurant charging premium prices, the experience should be much better. 2 stars.

Good seafood but at a premium
Apr 2026 • Couples
Located along the beachfront stretch on the southeastern end of Phu Quoc—anchored by the JW Marriott and surrounded by a cluster of upscale hotels and holiday rentals—Ann’s Seafood sits squarely in one of the island’s more developed (and tourist-oriented) pockets. You’re paying for the setting as much as the food here.

That said, the seafood delivers.

We ordered a mix of dishes including shrimp and squid, and everything was fresh and well-prepared. Nothing overly complex, but solid execution across the board—clean flavors, properly cooked, and exactly what you’d hope for from a beachfront seafood spot. Service was another highlight: prompt, friendly, and attentive without being intrusive.

The main consideration is value. Our late lunch came to about 2.6M VND (~$97 USD) with no alcohol, which is noticeably higher than what you’d pay elsewhere on the island for similar fare. That premium clearly reflects the location and surrounding resort ecosystem.

Bottom line: Fresh, reliable seafood in a convenient and polished beachfront setting—but at a price point that aligns more with the nearby luxury resorts than local dining spots. Worth it if you’re staying in the area or prioritizing convenience and ambiance; less compelling if you’re seeking the best value on the island.

Disappointing
Mar 2026 • Couples
Below average food in a country known for its delicious fresh produce & cuisine. expensive for the bad quality. Crunchy King prawns looked nothing like the description picture - pic on menu showed a light - sparse tempura style batter, they were actually coated in a VERY thick packet style bread crumb & very ordinary with a bottled sauce. Grilled squid was dry & sauce nothing like the sauces that we’ve had in all parts of Vietnam with squid. Shaking beef was tough & gristly… but the actual sauce was good… the dish had a side of dry stale unseasoned French fries - Why? The dish gave a “modified for tourists” vibe. Bok Choy with mushrooms was good, steamed rice ok … how could you muck that up though? We went as Google reviews were 4.8 by nearly 3000 reviewers, but clearly should’ve checked trip advisor, not holding much hope for the food in Phu Quoc, I hope I’m wrong. 
AVOID
